systematic_mappings.from: Python `ast.parse` + `ast.walk` over `sorted(root.rglob('*.py'))`, with `_imported_modules` resolving a relative import against the file's own package name and recording both a `from` import's base module and every one of its aliases as a candidate module
systematic_mappings.to: `test/testkit/ast.ts`'s `importedModules` (D-0504), shared with `test/messagebus/import-graph.test.ts`, `test/canary/structural.test.ts` and `test/secretary/structural.test.ts`, over a recursive directory walk of `.ts` files with an explicit declared allowlist for non-TypeScript artifacts (`docs/test-translation-conventions.md` section 10)
systematic_mappings.why: TypeScript has no package-dotted namespace; `importedModules` resolves a relative specifier to an absolute path instead, which asks the source's question (does this leave the package, and what does it reach?) without one. `namesASessionBackend` is the source's `_names_a_session_backend`, name for name, applied to the resolved path's segments; `knowsASessionBackend` is `_knows_a_session_backend`, applied to path containment under `src/session/` rather than a dotted-string prefix, with the same S1-contract exclusion.

target_only_tests.why: The directory walks in this file are LISTINGS, not hand-written lists (the source's own `rglob('*.py')`), so a `.ts` file with no `.py` analogue still gets a case: `src/control_plane/connection.ts`, `python_json.ts`, `python_repr.ts`, `refusals.ts` and `spike.ts` are helpers this port split into their own modules where the source keeps the equivalent logic inline elsewhere, and `test/control_plane/differential-oracle.test.ts` is a target-only structural check this port added with no source counterpart. `src/control_plane/cli.ts` and `test/control_plane/db-cli.test.ts` join them for a different reason and it is worth stating: they are the `continuo db create|migrate|verify` mount, which interlock has no counterpart for at all (it mounts no `db` subtree), so there is no source case to port and the walk picks them up exactly as it is meant to. `src/control_plane/run_lifecycle.ts` and `test/control_plane/run-lifecycle.test.ts` join for the third reason: they are `D-0046`'s single in-place writer of `run.status` and its suite, a continuo decision with no interlock counterpart (interlock has no fenced run writer at all), so again there is no source case to port. `src/control_plane/run_admission.ts`, `src/control_plane/run_cli.ts` and `test/control_plane/run-admission.test.ts` join for that same third reason one decision later: they are `D-0051`'s run-creation writer, its `continuo run admit` mount and their suite, and interlock has neither an admission writer nor a `run` subtree to port from. `src/control_plane/run_close.ts` and `test/control_plane/run-close.test.ts` join for that same third reason one lap later: they are `D-0084`'s `continuo run close`, the operator's record of a run reaching a terminal status, and interlock has neither a close verb nor a `run` subtree to port from. `src/control_plane/lap_run_intent.ts` and `test/control_plane/lap-run-intent.test.ts` join for the third reason once more: they are `D-0055`'s `LapRunIntent`, the lap-scoped execution intent `run admit` now takes and persists as `run_delegation_recorded`, and interlock has no delegation record of any kind to port from. Each is still exercised by the same property (no session-backend import), which is the point of walking rather than listing.

entries.target_id: test/gate_item11/no-provider-detail-leaks.test.ts::no shipped module knows both a provider and the control plane
entries.reason: Same assertion, walking the whole of `src/` instead of a dotted-prefix scan, with one deliberate exception the source has no counterpart for: `src/index.ts` is allowlisted (D-1001). continuo ships one package entry point (D-0002, `exports` restricted to `.`), so the single barrel re-exports both `./control_plane/*.js` and `./session/index.js` (which itself re-exports both providers) -- a shape the source's per-directory `__init__.py` package layout never produces, since nothing there re-exports both vocabularies from one module. The falsifier is recorded in D-1001: a subpath-exports split (`./control_plane`, `./session`) that let a provider swap avoid touching `src/index.ts`'s session half would remove the need for this exception.
